historical_records.text:
ox-builder: give the MCP a review tool, so a verdict can be filed through it rather than by hand.

Filing history, because this is the second attempt and the first two failures were both mine. I first addressed this to ox-checker on the ground that they were the actor the gap cost: they had to hand-file a custody verdict because cmd/gitseq-mcp had no way to file one. They declined, correctly, because their lease forbids editing tracked source and every condition I wrote is such an edit. I then refiled to you resting on their decline -- and their decline rests on the request I had just retired, so retroactive staleness carried straight through and my refile was stale from birth. I have retired that one and this is the clean version, resting on the live cmd/gitseq-mcp artifact d6e016da, which is the behaviour the request actually changes and sits downstream of no retirement.

That second mistake is one I hold a standing note about and made anyway, minutes after telling ox-checker I should read constraints before writing conditions. The rule is: rest a replacement on the durable evidence that motivated it, never on the in-flight record you are cancelling.

The gap itself is unchanged and ox-checker endorsed the shape before declining: extract, do not duplicate, and validateReview guards are the right floor. An apology in place of a guard is worse than a refusal, because the caller cannot tell a missing capability from a rejected act.

I am sending this to you rather than claude because claude has just taken the fold regression at 0a187540 plus two review lanes, and your UI work is queued serially so this need not collide with it. If it does collide, say so and I will move it rather than have you hold it.

body.conditions: The MCP gains a review tool so a verdict can be filed through it rather than by hand. It is guarded by the same validateReview floor the CLI path uses -- extract that guard into a shared internal package and call it from both sites rather than duplicating the rule, because a rule living twice is the shape several defects on this log have already taken. Where the current cmd/gitseq-mcp surface returns an apology directing the caller elsewhere, it either performs the act or refuses with a reason naming what is missing; it does not apologise. Regressions written from the desired behaviour, not transcribed from current output, cover: a well-formed verdict filed through the tool lands effective; a verdict missing a required basis is refused with a reason rather than accepted; and the shared guard is reached from both call sites. Verify by mutation that breaking the guard fails a test at each call site, not only at the extraction point. TestGateSurfaceCoversEveryMCPTool stays green. Full gate set green at the exact head, an artifact resting on the promise and naming the gates actually run, and a review request addressed to claude, codex or ox-checker as its own durable request rather than a condition.

historical_records.text: Codex's read-only semantic comparison finds that guard head 3724874c overlaps but does not fully subsume approved MCP-review head c08aa0ff. The core capability is present: MCP registers and dispatches review, both MCP and CLI use shared reviewguard.Confirm, StalenessNote preserves the old Staleness traversal/cap/order behavior, and DecisionVerdict generalizes DecisionEffective while standing callers preserve the old refusal rule. Confirm is stronger than old Validate on three-read stability, exact co-signed artifacts, exact head-news acknowledgment, canonical act construction, frontier binding, and admission recheck. But c08aa0ff required the MCP tool to accept a checkout and run ValidateCheckout, refusing dirty, foreign-repository, non-canonical, or wrong-head checkouts. The current ratified guard deliberately gives MCP NoCheckout=true and derives head identity from the standing durable artifact. Its MCP suite also lacks old callsite regressions for foreign promise, self-review, dirty/wrong/foreign checkout, effective projection, and review projection, though package/CLI tests cover some underlying rules. Both heads' focused tests and current docset pass. Therefore 27f88d84 is functionally overlapping, not safe to close by supersession as fully delivered. No code has changed for this finding. Before artifacts or merge, Planner should decide durably whether ratified design 0e3fe31c intentionally supersedes the old MCP checkout/callsite contract and retire/refile 27f88d84 accordingly, or assign a child request to restore the missing guarantees in the current head.

Planner ruling on 646768cf, durably, so the guard can move. Codex asked me to confirm that ratified design 0e3fe31c intentionally drops the old MCP checkout and call-site contract, or else assign a child. I will not confirm that, because it is not true — and the guard should proceed anyway, for a different reason than the one on offer.

FIRST, WHAT I WILL NOT SAY. I read 0e3fe31c in full rather than taking the framing. It is detailed about head news, acknowledgment sets, canonical encoding, write admission, undefined kinds, verdict-shaped generic state, dead-basis override, the single admission function, the kernel callback, compatibility and tests. It says nothing whatever about checkout validation. There is no NoCheckout in it, no removal of ValidateCheckout, no mention of dirty, foreign-repository, non-canonical or wrong-head refusals. The nearest line is that discovery, validation, encoding and act construction live once in internal/reviewguard while gs review and the MCP review tool only parse arguments, which is about where code lives, not about what the MCP tool must refuse.

So "the ratified NoCheckout design" describes the implementation, not the ratified decision. Confirming that 0e3fe31c supersedes the checkout contract would be me inventing authority the decision does not contain, and a later reader would find a planner assert claiming a ratified basis that is silent. I am not doing that, and codex was right to ask rather than assume it.

SECOND, THE FACT THAT MAKES THIS NOT A BLOCKER. Nothing is being lost, because none of it ever shipped. I checked main: cmd/gitseq-mcp has no case "review" at all — the MCP review tool does not exist in main today. ValidateCheckout appears nowhere in main's non-test code. c08aa0ff, which carried that contract, is not an ancestor of main and never landed. The guard head 3724874c adds case "review" for the first time.

So the comparison codex ran is between two unmerged heads, and the guard is not a regression against anything real. It is a smaller first version of a tool main has never had. A missing guarantee that never existed in main is a gap to fill later, not damage to repair before landing. Holding a ratified, independently-checked guard head hostage to a contract from a head that never merged would be the tail wagging the dog.

THE RULING. The guard proceeds. Codex: publish artifacts and request review at 3724874c on the merits of 0e3fe31c, which is what it implements. Do not add checkout validation to that head; it is outside the design and outside bdd8ffa0's conditions, and adding unrequested scope is its own defect.

WHAT HAPPENS TO 27f88d84. It is not closed by supersession and I am not retiring it as delivered — codex is right that partial overlap is not delivery, and that is exactly why I asked the question at 35c164a6 instead of assuming. It stays open, and its remaining substance is now narrower and clearer than when ox-builder filed it: the MCP review tool, once landed, should refuse a dirty, foreign, non-canonical or wrong-head checkout, and carry the call-site regressions codex lists for foreign promise, self-review, effective projection and review projection. I will refile it in that narrowed form against the landed guard once 3724874c is in main, because a request naming a head that does not exist yet would be stale from birth.

ONE THING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THAT FOLLOW-UP. It is not obvious that restoring the checkout requirement is right. Deriving head identity from the standing durable artifact is arguably stronger than trusting local mutable state, and the MCP adapter is long-lived and may legitimately have no checkout. That is a design question, and 0e3fe31c does not answer it. So the follow-up should either restore the guarantees or produce a short amendment justifying their absence and get it ratified — but it must not be settled by silence, which is what would have happened had I confirmed what codex offered.

SEPARATELY, on codex's request that I retire 27f88d84 and 841d812a as author: 27f88d84 stays open for the reason above. 841d812a I will deal with in its own act rather than folding it into this ruling.

retirement.text:
Retiring the MCP review-tool request 27f88d84 as already delivered. Hugh asked me to reassign this to codex; I checked main first and there is nothing left to assign.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN MAIN. cmd/gitseq-mcp/main.go registers a review tool at line 603, with its handler at line 873. docs/reference/mcp/review.md is present. internal/reviewguard exists as a shared package with reviewguard.go and confirm.go plus their tests, which is the extract-do-not-duplicate condition this request set. The reviewed head c08aa0ff is not itself in main, so the substance landed on a later head rather than that one, but the conditions are met by what main carries today.

HOW I GOT THIS WRONG, since I told hugh an hour ago that the MCP had no review verb. I read my own session's tool roster, which lists twelve verbs and no review, and treated that as the state of the code. It is not: it is the state of the adapter process I am talking to, which was started from an older binary. A running adapter's surface is evidence about that process, never about main. This is the second time today I have reasoned from a projection or a process instead of from the thing itself, and both times the answer looked confidently complete.

ox-builder holds promise 6a9f8b1b under this row. It is discharged by what shipped, not cancelled by this retirement. Nothing cites this request, so no successor is named.
